outcome: Use of decision aids when counselling patients
Comfort levels offering oxytocin induction for TOLAC
Comfort levels offering cervical foley or amniotomy for TOLAC
Comfort levels offering TOLAC to patients with an unknown uterine scar
Comfort levels offering TOLAC to patients with more than 1 previous cesarean delivery

Incidence of litigation resulting from uterine rupture cases
cohort: The study participants were 381 practicing obstetrical care providers (obstetrician-gynaecologists, family physicians, and midwives) with an office antenatal practice across every Canadian province and territory.
finding: Most Canadian obstetrical care providers actively encourage TOLAC, but comfort levels vary significantly based on induction methods, patient history, and geographic region, with a minority consistently using decision aids despite acknowledging their utility.
mod_finding: The study revealed varied comfort levels among providers regarding offering TOLAC based on specific induction methods (oxytocin vs. cervical foley/amniotomy) and patient history (unknown uterine scar, more than one previous cesarean delivery).
cross-section timing: The survey captured current attitudes and practice patterns around 2021, prior to its publication in 2022.
